speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mucinous Ovarian Tumor with Endometrial Hyperplasia.

The combination of a complex adnexal mass, thickened endometrium, and normal tumor markers (excluding CA-125 which was requested earlier but results aren't explicitly detailed as elevated here, though the MRI confirms the structural findings) suggests a primary ovarian neoplasm. Given the solid/cystic nature and patient age, malignancy must be ruled out despite normal CEA/CA19-9. The thickened endometrium is a direct consequence of the unopposed estrogen likely produced by the granulosa cell component or simply a coincidental hyperplasia in the setting of postmenopausal bleeding. I recommend proceeding with surgical exploration for definitive histopathological diagnosis.
